.claude/reference/scope/prompt-mode/mode-system-prompts/index.md:52:- that Suspense adds each mode's instructions to a prompt itself, in a block marked <task-instructions> at its head, and the spec's references and the understanding file with them, so a prompt written for a mode is only what the user wants done, in the user's own terms, and never holds a <task-instructions> block, steps the mode already takes, or instructions about building, checking, the understanding file, or the verdict line a task ends its reply with
.claude/reference/scope/prompt-mode/mode-system-prompts/index.md:71:Every question is told how an answer hands back prompts and questions in the forms the [AskConversation](../ask-conversation/index.md#ask-conversation) shows as cards, so whenever the user asks for a prompt, it comes back as a card they can send to Code, Chain, or Spec. It is not a project's to edit or leave out: the application adds it to each question's <task-instructions> block, after the project's Ask instructions, on a paragraph of its own, whatever those say, including a project's Ask instructions saved before it was added, which are kept as they are. Its text is baked into the application from this application's own repository, in `ask-cards.md` in its `.suspense/system-prompts` directory beside the defaults, and a build can't be made without it. It is never given to a task, and Freeform sends nothing. It says:
.claude/reference/scope/prompt-mode/mode-system-prompts/index.md:74:## Verdict
.claude/reference/scope/prompt-mode/mode-system-prompts/index.md:76:Every task is asked to end its reply with a verdict saying whether it did the work, so the application can tell a task that couldn't from one that did by reading one line, never by guessing from the wording of its reply, as the [HarnessIntegration](../../harness-integration/index.md#harness-integration)'s failures say. It is not a project's to edit or leave out: the application adds it to the <task-instructions> block of every Code, Chain, and Spec task, a Chain prompt's code step and spec follow-up and a Code task sent to Spec included, last, after the project's instructions and any injected prompt, on a paragraph of its own, whatever those say, including a project's instructions saved before it was added, which are kept as they are. Its text is baked into the application from this application's own repository, in `task-verdict.md` in its `.suspense/system-prompts` directory beside the defaults, and a build can't be made without it. It is never given to a question, nor to a resumed task's resume message, and Freeform sends nothing, so a Freeform task gives no verdict. It says:
.claude/reference/scope/prompt-mode/mode-system-prompts/index.md:77:After your reply, end with one line of its own that is exactly `SUSPENSE-VERDICT: done` if you did the work this prompt asks for, or exactly `SUSPENSE-VERDICT: failed` if you couldn't: if you failed, couldn't write or change what you were to, were blocked by the sandbox, a missing file, or anything else, or gave up. When it is failed, say in your reply, before that line, what stopped you. Write nothing after that line.
.claude/reference/scope/harness-integration/index.md:38:A result no longer ends the task on its own. The run's last result is the first to come once every message sent has been taken in and no background task is still going. A result that comes before then, while a message sent hasn't been taken in or a background task is still going, is only an answer: the task keeps running, its input stays open, and more can still be sent to it. At the last result the run's input is closed, but the task is only shown as finished once the harness's process has exited as well, and it then finishes in the state of that last result, unless its reply's verdict says it failed, when it finishes Failed, as the failures say; until the process exits, the task keeps running. A process that exits without a last result finishes the task as a run with no result does, failed. A run that is stopped closes its input and ends straight away, whatever is still going in the background, since its whole process group is ended with it.
.claude/reference/scope/harness-integration/index.md:62:A task's run can also fail without any error from the harness, when its reply says it couldn't do the work: that it failed, that it couldn't write or change what it was to, that the sandbox or a missing file blocked it, or that it gave up. Such a task is Failed, never Done. This is never guessed from the wording of the reply: the run says it in its verdict, a line every task is asked to end its reply with, as the [ModeSystemPrompts](../prompt-mode/mode-system-prompts/index.md#mode-system-prompts) says, and the application reads only that. The verdict is the last line of the reply of the run's last result that isn't blank, trimmed, and read without regard to case, either `SUSPENSE-VERDICT: done` where it did the work, or `SUSPENSE-VERDICT: failed` where it didn't. Where that line reads failed, the task finishes Failed, with the "Failed" label of the [MessageListStatus](../prompt-mode/message-list/Status.md#message-list-status), though the harness reported success. Where it reads done, or the reply gives no verdict, as a Freeform task's, the task finishes in the state of its last result, as the feeding says; a verdict never makes a run that failed Done.
.claude/reference/scope/harness-integration/index.md:63:A task failed by its verdict says why in the run's own words, as every failed run does: its output shows its reply, which says what stopped it, beneath a heading saying the run reported that it couldn't do the work. The verdict line itself is never shown in a task's output, nor handed on as part of its final output, to a chain's next step or anywhere else. The task is saved as Failed in its history record, its reply with it, so it reads Failed after a restart too, and never Done.

content.text:
I couldn't fix the build error: the fix is a file this session can't write. Nothing in `src` needed changing.

The error comes from `task_verdict()` in `src/system_prompts.rs:83`, which bakes in `.suspense/system-prompts/task-verdict.md`, and that file doesn't exist. The spec says the verdict text comes from that file and that a build can't be made without it ([Verdict](.claude/reference/scope/prompt-mode/mode-system-prompts/index.md#verdict)). So the fix is to create the file, not to put the text in the code. Writing it failed with "permission denied" both through the shell (even outside the sandbox) and through the file tool, because this run has no access to `.suspense/system-prompts`.

To fix it, create `.suspense/system-prompts/task-verdict.md` with the text the spec quotes:

```
After your reply, end with one line of its own that is exactly `SUSPENSE-VERDICT: done` if you did the work this prompt asks for, or exactly `SUSPENSE-VERDICT: failed` if you couldn't: if you failed, couldn't write or change what you were to, were blocked by the sandbox, a missing file, or anything else, or gave up. When it is failed, say in your reply, before that line, what stopped you. Write nothing after that line.
```

I can't confirm the build passes after that. In this session the other prompt files in that directory (`system.md`, `code.md`, `ask-cards.md` and so on) are also unreadable, so `cargo build` stops on those here. Of all of them, only `task-verdict.md` is actually missing.

The error comes from `task_verdict()` in `src/system_prompts.rs:83`, which bakes in `.suspense/system-prompts/task-verdict.md`, and that file doesn't exist. The spec says the verdict text comes from that file and that a build can't be made without it ([Verdict](.claude/reference/scope/prompt-mode/mode-system-prompts/index.md#verdict)). So the fix is to create the file, not to put the text in the code. Writing it failed with "permission denied" both through the shell (even outside the sandbox) and through the file tool, because this run has no access to `.suspense/system-prompts`.

To fix it, create `.suspense/system-prompts/task-verdict.md` with the text the spec quotes:

```
After your reply, end with one line of its own that is exactly `SUSPENSE-VERDICT: done` if you did the work this prompt asks for, or exactly `SUSPENSE-VERDICT: failed` if you couldn't: if you failed, couldn't write or change what you were to, were blocked by the sandbox, a missing file, or anything else, or gave up. When it is failed, say in your reply, before that line, what stopped you. Write nothing after that line.
```

I can't confirm the build passes after that. In this session the other prompt files in that directory (`system.md`, `code.md`, `ask-cards.md` and so on) are also unreadable, so `cargo build` stops on those here. Of all of them, only `task-verdict.md` is actually missing.
